title: Marketing food to young people
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers general linked youth health issues and where young people live, not how food companies market unhealthy food to young people, so no bank point teaches this idea.

draft.title: Marketing food to young people
card: Food companies aim their advertising at young people because young people influence what they and their families buy, and they may keep buying a brand for years.
Companies use social media, games and influencers, who are people with a large online following. An influencer who shows a snack in a video can make it seem popular and normal.
Companies sponsor sports teams, events and school activities. This links the brand with fun, sport and friends.
Bright colours, cartoon characters and free toys on packaging attract children. These methods are often used for less healthy foods that are high in sugar, salt or saturated fat.
draft.remember: Companies use online, sponsorship and packaging methods that often promote less healthy foods.

a.q: Why do food companies target young people with their marketing?
opts: Young people sway family purchases and may stay loyal
Young people are the only group who buy packaged food
Young people are legally required to buy the products
Young people can judge the health claims better than adults
a.why: Young people influence what families buy and may stay loyal to a brand as they grow up. They are not the only buyers of packaged food, so that option is too strong.
a.clue: Think about who gains from a brand being loved early.

b.q: A soft drink company pays a popular streamer to drink its product during a live game stream watched by many teenagers. Which marketing method is this?
opts: Sponsorship of a local sports team
A health claim on the front of the label
b.why: The company pays a person with a large online following to show its product, which is influencer marketing on social media. It is not sponsorship of a team or event, and nothing here involves packaging.
b.clue: Who is showing the product, and where?

a.best: Young people sway family purchases and may stay loyal
